tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: TaskCreate
tools.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

tools.name: TaskGet
tools.description:
Use this tool to retrieve a task by its ID from the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- When you need the full description and context before starting work on a task
- To understand task dependencies (what it blocks, what blocks it)
- After being assigned a task, to get complete requirements

## Output

Returns full task details:
- **subject**: Task title
- **description**: Detailed requirements and context
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **blocks**: Tasks waiting on this one to complete
- **blockedBy**: Tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Tips

- After fetching a task, verify its blockedBy list is empty before beginning work.
- Use TaskList to see all tasks in summary form.

tools.name: TaskList
tools.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop

- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id

- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

tools.name: TaskUpdate
tools.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it

**Update task details:**

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Web search results for query: "Airtable NocoDB row click open properties panel sidebar UX pattern"

I'll search for information about this UX pattern used in Airtable, NocoDB, and similar tools.

## Search Results Summary

**Row Click → Properties Panel/Sidebar UX Pattern in Airtable & NocoDB**

This is a well-established UX pattern in spreadsheet/database UI tools:

### How it works:
- **Airtable**: Clicking the **row expander icon** (appears on hover at the left of each row) opens a full **record detail panel** — either as a modal overlay or side panel — showing all fields for that record in a vertical form layout
- **NocoDB**: Implements a similar **"expand row"** feature where clicking a row expand icon opens a side drawer/panel showing all column fields as a form, allowing editing without leaving the grid view

### Key UX Characteristics:
- **Trigger**: Usually an expand icon (⤢ or similar) on row hover, or double-clicking the row
- **Panel type**: Modal dialog OR sliding sidebar/drawer (right-side panel)
- **Content**: Displays all fields in a vertical stacked form layout
- **Non-destructive**: Grid view remains visible/accessible behind the panel
- **Keyboard nav**: Supports prev/next record navigation arrows within the panel

### Related terminology seen in the wild:
- "Row expand" / "Expand record"
- "Record detail panel"
- "Side peek" (used by Notion)
- "Record inspector"
- Field properties sidebar (more common in form builders)

This pattern is now standard in tools like **Airtable, NocoDB, Baserow, Notion, Retool, and Appsmith**.

## Search Results Summary

Based on the web search for **"Notion database table view UX pattern click row to open detail sidebar 2024"**, here are the key findings:

---

### Key UX Patterns Found

**Notion's Core Interaction Model:**
- Notion's database table view uses a **"peek" pattern** — clicking a row opens a **side panel/sidebar** (called a "page peek") that slides in from the right, showing the full page content without losing context of the table.
- Users can also open records in **full page view** or a **centered modal** — toggling between these is a common UX discussion point in 2024 Notion communities.

**2024 UX Trends Around This Pattern:**
- The **"master-detail" layout** (list/table on left, detail panel on right) has become a dominant SaaS pattern, heavily influenced by Notion, Linear, and Airtable.
- Tools like **Linear** popularized the sidebar detail view for issue tracking, which many teams replicate.
- Notion introduced **"side peek" as default** for database items in recent updates, reinforcing this as a standard expectation.

**Community Feedback (2024):**
- Highly requested: ability to **resize the peek sidebar**.
- Debate around click vs. dedicated icon to trigger peek vs. full-page open.
- Developers building Notion-like tools frequently reference this pattern in threads on Reddit, Hacker News, and UX forums.

**Implementation References:**
- Libraries like **TanStack Table** + custom drawer/sheet components are commonly used to replicate this pattern.
- Shadcn/ui's `Sheet` component is frequently cited for building the sidebar detail panel.

input.content:
# Plan: Notion-Style Table + Right Sidebar Field Editor

**File**: `ui-test-standalone.html`  
**Date**: 2026-10-12  
**Problem**: The current UI stacks every field's editor cards vertically — noisy, confusing, hard to scan at a glance.  
**Goal**: The main view looks like a clean Notion/Airtable table (column headers + rows of cells). Clicking any row opens its field editor detail in a right sidebar that slides in. No accordion cards, no color-coded sections in the main view.

---

## Research Findings

### Industry Pattern: Master-Detail / Side Peek

| Tool | Table UX | Click Action | Detail UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Notion** | Grid with typed column headers | Row → "Side peek" slides from right | Full page or right panel |
| **Airtable** | Spreadsheet grid | Hover → expand icon ⤢ → modal or side drawer | Stacked form layout |
| **NocoDB** | Spreadsheet grid | Expand row icon → right drawer | Labeled field form |
| **Linear** | Issue list | Click row → right panel | Properties panel |

**Common denominator:**
1. Grid/table = read-only scan surface. Each column = one field type. Each row = one record/entity.
2. Click → the detail panel slides in from the right with the full editable form for that row.
3. Table stays visible (behind or alongside the panel).
4. No color-coded sections or accordion cards cluttering main view.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┐
│  HEADER (title, tabs, toolbar)   │                               │
├──────────────────────────────────┤                               │
│  TABLE (Notion-style)            │   FIELD EDITOR SIDEBAR        │
│  ┌──┬──────────┬──────┬───────┐ │   (slides in on row click)    │
│  │  │ Col Name │ Type │ Slug  │ │                               │
│  ├──┼──────────┼──────┼───────┤ │   ▸ Column Name input         │

│  │  │ Username │ 📝   │ user… │ │   ▸ Metadata (prefix/opts...) │
│  │  │ Email    │ 📝   │ email │ │   ▸ Slug input                │
│  └──┴──────────┴──────┴───────┘ │   ▸ Delete button             │
│  + Add Field row                 │                               │
└──────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Main area**: full-width when sidebar closed; shrinks to ~60% when sidebar open.
- **Sidebar**: fixed 380px wide, slides in with CSS `transform: translateX(100%)` → `translateX(0)`. Overlaps on mobile.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- Close: `✕` button top-right, or click outside table.

- Table rows: subtle hover background tint.

- All data model (`MOCK_DATA`, `FIELD_TYPES`, `tables`, mutation functions).
- Inspector panel (SQL/JSON code view) — relocated into the sidebar as a tab within it.
- Quick-add field type buttons — relocated to a row at the bottom of the table (`+ icon row`).
- Filter bar — relocated to toolbar above the table.
- Toast notification system — unchanged.
- Theme toggle — unchanged.

6. **JS — `navigateSidebar(dir)`**: Prev/next arrow navigation.
7. **JS — Drag tokens**: Kept for the compact column-order chip strip above the table.

```
pk:      #38bdf8  (blue)
text:    #10b981  (green)
```

      border: 1px solid var(--border-light);
      border-radius: var(--radius-md);
      color: var(--text-primary);
      font-family: var(--font-body);
      font-size: 14px;
      transition: all 0.12s ease;
      resize: none;
      width: 100%;
    }

    input[type="text"]:focus,
    input[type="email"]:focus,
    input[type="number"]:focus,
    select:focus,
    textarea:focus {
      background: var(--bg-input-focus);
      border-color: var(--accent);
      box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-glow);
      outline: none;
    }

    textarea {
      height: 90px;
      padding: 0.65rem 0.85rem;
      font-size: 13px;
      line-height: 1.5;
    }

    select {
      appearance: none;
      background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg width='8' height='6' viewBox='0 0 8 6' fill='none' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%3E%3Cpath d='M1 1L4 4L7 1' stroke='%23ff9e1b' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round'/%3E%3C/svg%3E");
      background-repeat: no-repeat;
      background-position: right 10px center;
      padding-right: 2rem;
      cursor: pointer;
    }

    /* Enum options */
    .options-list {
      display: flex;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
      gap: 0.4rem;
    }

    .option-pill {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 0.35rem;
      background: var(--accent-bg);
      border: 1px solid rgba(255,158,27,0.3);
      color: var(--accent);
      padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem;
      border-radius: 4px;
      font-size: 12.5px;
      font-weight: 500;
    }

    .option-pill button {
      background: none;
      border: none;
      color: var(--accent);
      cursor: pointer;
      font-size: 11px;
      padding: 0;
      line-height: 1;
      opacity: 0.7;
    }

    .option-pill button:hover { opacity: 1; }

    /* Section divider */
    .section-sep {
      height: 1px;
      background: var(--border-light);
    }

    /* Sidebar footer */
    .sidebar-footer {
      flex-shrink: 0;
      padding: 1rem 1.25rem;
      border-top: 1px solid var(--border-light);
    }

    /* Code view (inspector) */
    .code-block {
      background: var(--bg-input);
      border: 1px solid var(--border-light);
      border-radius: var(--radius-md);
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .code-block-head {
      padding: 0.5rem 0.85rem;
      background: rgba(255,255,255,0.02);
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-light);
      font: 600 11px var(--font-mono);
      color: var(--text-dim);
      text-transform: uppercase;
      display: flex;
      justify-content: space-between;
      align-items: center;
    }

    .code-pre {
      padding: 0.85rem;
      font-family: var(--font-mono);
      font-size: 11.5px;
      line-height: 1.55;
      color: var(--text-secondary);
      overflow-x: auto;
      max-height: 380px;
      overflow-y: auto;
      white-space: pre;
    }

    /* ========================================================================
       TOAST
       ======================================================================== */
    .toast {
      position: fixed;
      bottom: 1.5rem;
      right: 1.5rem;
      background: var(--accent);
      color: #0a0908;
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: 13px;
      padding: 0.7rem 1.25rem;
      border-radius: var(--radius-md);
      box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
      z-index: 99999;
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateY(8px);
      pointer-events: none;
      transition: all 0.22s ease;
    }

    .toast.show { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }

    /* ========================================================================
       SCROLLBAR STYLING
       ======================================================================== */
    ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 6px; height: 6px; }
    ::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: transparent; }
    ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--border-mid); border-radius: 3px; }
    ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover { background: var(--text-dim); }

    /* ========================================================================
       RESPONSIVE
       ======================================================================== */
    @media (max-width: 768px) {
      :root { --sidebar-width: 100vw; }
      .field-sidebar.open { width: 100vw; position: fixed; right: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0; z-index: 200; }
    }
  </style>
</head>

<body>
<div class="app-shell">

  <!-- ======= HEADER ======= -->
  <header class="app-header">
    <div class="app-title">
      <span>Project</span>
      <span class="badge">Entry</span>
    </div>
    <div class="header-divider"></div>

    <!-- Table tabs -->
    <nav class="table-tabs" id="table-tabs"></nav>

    <div class="header-actions">
      <button class="btn primary" onclick="saveTable()">💾 Save</button>
      <button class="btn" onclick="syncSqlite()">⚡ Sync</button>
      <button class="btn" onclick="toggleTheme()">🌓</button>
    </div>
  </header>

  <!-- ======= TOOLBAR ======= -->
  <div class="toolbar" id="toolbar">
    <span class="toolbar-label">Filter</span>
    <div id="filter-bar"></div>
    <div class="toolbar-divider"></div>
    <span class="toolbar-label">Order</span>
    <div class="token-strip" id="token-strip"></div>
    <div style="margin-left: auto; display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center;">
      <span id="col-count-label" style="font: 500 12px var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim);"></span>
      <span style="font: 500 12px var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim);">·</span>
      <span style="font: 500 11px var(--font-body); color: var(--text-tertiary); cursor: pointer;" id="table-name-display" onclick="promptRenameTable()"></span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- ======= WORKSPACE ======= -->
  <div class="workspace">

    <!-- Table area -->
    <div class="table-area" id="table-area">
      <table class="notion-table" id="notion-table">
        <colgroup>
          <col><col><col><col><col><col>
        </colgroup>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>#</th>
            <th>Column Name</th>
            <th>Type</th>
            <th>Slug</th>
            <th>SQL Type</th>
            <th></th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody id="table-body"></tbody>
      </table>
    </div>

    <!-- Field editor sidebar -->
    <aside class="field-sidebar" id="field-sidebar">
      <div class="sidebar-inner">

        <!-- Sidebar head -->
        <div class="sidebar-head">
          <div class="sidebar-head-row">
            <div class="sidebar-col-label" id="sidebar-col-label">
              <span class="col-num" id="sb-col-num">#1</span>
              <span id="sb-col-icon"></span>
              <span class="col-title" id="sb-col-title">Column</span>
            </div>
            <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem;">
              <div class="sidebar-nav">
                <button class="btn ghost icon-only sm" onclick="navigateSidebar(-1)" title="Previous column">◀</button>
                <button class="btn ghost icon-only sm" onclick="navigateSidebar(1)" title="Next column">▶</button>
              </div>
              <button class="btn ghost icon-only" onclick="closeSidebar()" title="Close (Esc)">✕</button>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="sidebar-tabs">
            <button class="stab-btn active" onclick="switchSidebarTab('edit', this)">Edit</button>
            <button class="stab-btn" onclick="switchSidebarTab('sql', this)">SQL</button>
            <button class="stab-btn" onclick="switchSidebarTab('json', this)">JSON</button>
          </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Sidebar body -->
        <div class="sidebar-body">

          <!-- Edit panel -->
          <div class="sidebar-panel active" id="sp-edit">

            <div class="field-group">
              <label class="field-label">Column Name</label>
              <input type="text" id="sb-name" placeholder="e.g. User ID"
                oninput="sbUpdateName(this.value)">
            </div>

            <div class="field-group">
              <label class="field-label">Slug <span class="field-hint">(database key)</span></label>
              <input type="text" id="sb-slug" placeholder="e.g. user_id"
                style="font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 13px;"
                oninput="sbUpdateSlug(this.value)">
            </div>

            <div class="field-group">
              <label class="field-label">Field Type</label>
              <select id="sb-type" onchange="sbUpdateType(this.value)"></select>
            </div>

            <div class="section-sep"></div>

            <!-- Dynamic metadata section -->
            <div id="sb-meta"></div>

          </div>

          <!-- SQL panel -->
          <div class="sidebar-panel" id="sp-sql">
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-block-head">
                <span id="sql-title">CREATE TABLE</span>
                <button class="btn sm ghost" onclick="copyCode('sql-code')">📋 Copy</button>
              </div>
              <pre class="code-pre" id="sql-code"></pre>
            </div>
          </div>

          <!-- JSON panel -->
          <div class="sidebar-panel" id="sp-json">
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-block-head">
                <span id="json-title">JSON Schema</span>
                <button class="btn sm ghost" onclick="copyCode('json-code')">📋 Copy</button>
              </div>
              <pre class="code-pre" id="json-code"></pre>
            </div>
          </div>

        </div>

        <!-- Sidebar footer -->
        <div class="sidebar-footer">
          <button class="btn danger" style="width:100%;" onclick="sbDeleteColumn()">
            🗑 Delete Column
          </button>
        </div>

      </div>
    </aside>

  </div><!-- end .workspace -->

</div><!-- end .app-shell -->

<div class="toast" id="toast"></div>

<script>
/* ============================================================
   DATA MODEL
   ============================================================ */

const FIELD_TYPES = {
  hex_id:          { category: 'pk',      icon: '🔑', title: 'Hex ID',          sql: 'TEXT PRIMARY KEY' },
  text_single:     { category: 'text',    icon: '📝', title: 'Text (single)',    sql: 'TEXT' },
  text_multi:      { category: 'text',    icon: '📋', title: 'Text (multi)',     sql: 'TEXT' },
  int_scalar:      { category: 'scalar',  icon: '🔢', title: 'Integer',         sql: 'INTEGER' },
  float_scalar:    { category: 'scalar',  icon: '🔢', title: 'Float',           sql: 'REAL' },
  boolean:         { category: 'boolean', icon: '🔘', title: 'Boolean',         sql: 'INTEGER DEFAULT 0' },
  enum_single:     { category: 'enum',    icon: '🏷️', title: 'Enum (single)',   sql: 'TEXT' },
  enum_multi:      { category: 'enum',    icon: '🏷️', title: 'Enum (multi)',    sql: 'TEXT (JSON)' },
  relation_single: { category: 'rel',     icon: '🔗', title: 'Relation (→1)',   sql: 'TEXT' },
  relation_multi:  { category: 'rel',     icon: '🔗', title: 'Relation (→N)',   sql: 'TEXT (JSON)' },
};

const MOCK_DATA = {
  users: {
    table_name: 'users',
    columns: [
      { name: 'User ID',   slug: 'id',          type: 'hex_id',          metadata: { prefix: 'USER' } },
      { name: 'Username',  slug: 'username',     type: 'text_single',     metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Email',     slug: 'email',        type: 'text_single',     metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Bio',       slug: 'bio',          type: 'text_multi',      metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Age',       slug: 'age',          type: 'int_scalar',      metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Balance',   slug: 'balance',      type: 'float_scalar',    metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Active',    slug: 'is_active',    type: 'boolean',         metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Role',      slug: 'role',         type: 'enum_single',     metadata: { options: ['admin', 'editor', 'viewer'] } },
      { name: 'Tags',      slug: 'tags',         type: 'enum_multi',      metadata: { options: ['premium', 'verified', 'staff'] } },
      { name: 'Manager',   slug: 'manager_id',   type: 'relation_single', metadata: { target: 'users' } },
      { name: 'Projects',  slug: 'project_ids',  type: 'relation_multi',  metadata: { target: 'projects' } },
    ]
  },
  projects: {
    table_name: 'projects',
    columns: [
      { name: 'Project ID',   slug: 'id',          type: 'hex_id',          metadata: { prefix: 'PROJ' } },
      { name: 'Title',         slug: 'title',        type: 'text_single',     metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Description',   slug: 'description',  type: 'text_multi',      metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Budget',        slug: 'budget',        type: 'float_scalar',    metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Status',        slug: 'status',        type: 'enum_single',     metadata: { options: ['planning', 'active', 'completed'] } },
      { name: 'Public',        slug: 'is_public',     type: 'boolean',         metadata: {} },
      { name: 'Owner',         slug: 'owner_id',      type: 'relation_single', metadata: { target: 'users' } },
      { name: 'Team Members',  slug: 'member_ids',    type: 'relation_multi',  metadata: { target: 'users' } },
    ]
  }
};

let tables = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(MOCK_DATA));
let activeTable  = 'users';
let activeFilter = 'all';
let activeSidebarTab = 'edit';
let activeColIdx = null;   // currently selected column index

/* ============================================================
   INIT
   ============================================================ */
function init() {
  renderTableTabs();
  renderFilterBar();
  renderTable();
  renderTokenStrip();
  updateColCountLabel();

  // Keyboard: Escape closes sidebar
  document.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') closeSidebar();
    if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft'  && activeColIdx !== null) navigateSidebar(-1);
    if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' && activeColIdx !== null) navigateSidebar(1);
  });
}

/* ============================================================
   TABLE TABS
   ============================================================ */
function renderTableTabs() {
  const container = document.getElementById('table-tabs');
  const names = Object.keys(tables);
  container.innerHTML = names.map(name => `
    <button class="tab-btn ${name === activeTable ? 'active' : ''}" onclick="switchTable('${name}')">
      📁 ${name}
    </button>
  `).join('') + `
    <button class="tab-btn new-table" onclick="createTable()">+ New Table</button>
  `;
}

function switchTable(name) {
  if (!tables[name]) return;
  activeTable = name;
  activeColIdx = null;
  closeSidebar();
  renderTableTabs();
  renderFilterBar();
  renderTable();
  renderTokenStrip();
  updateColCountLabel();
}

function createTable() {
  const name = prompt('Table name (e.g., tasks, inventory):');
  if (!name) return;
  const clean = name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9_]/g, '_');
  if (tables[clean]) { alert('Table already exists'); return; }
  tables[clean] = {
    table_name: clean,
    columns: [{ name: 'ID', slug: 'id', type: 'hex_id', metadata: { prefix: clean.substring(0, 4).toUpperCase() } }]
  };
  switchTable(clean);
  showToast(`Created table "${clean}"`);
}

function promptRenameTable() {
  const current = tables[activeTable].table_name;
  const next = prompt('Rename table:', current);
  if (!next || next === current) return;
  const clean = next.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9_]/g, '_');
  tables[activeTable].table_name = clean;
  renderTable();
  document.getElementById('table-name-display').textContent = clean;
  showToast(`Renamed to "${clean}"`);
}

function updateColCountLabel() {
  const t = tables[activeTable];
  if (!t) return;
  document.getElementById('col-count-label').textContent = `${t.columns.length} columns`;
  document.getElementById('table-name-display').textContent = t.table_name;
}

/* ============================================================
   FILTER BAR
   ============================================================ */
function renderFilterBar() {
  const cats = ['all', 'pk', 'text', 'scalar', 'boolean', 'enum', 'rel'];
  const icons = { all: '📊', pk: '🔑', text: '📝', scalar: '🔢', boolean: '🔘', enum: '🏷️', rel: '🔗' };
  document.getElementById('filter-bar').innerHTML = cats.map(cat => `
    <button class="filter-btn ${cat === activeFilter ? 'active' : ''}" onclick="setFilter('${cat}')">
      ${icons[cat]} ${cat === 'all' ? 'All' : cat.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + cat.slice(1)}
    </button>
  `).join('');
}

function setFilter(cat) {
  activeFilter = cat;
  renderFilterBar();
  renderTable();
}

/* ============================================================
   MAIN TABLE RENDER
   ============================================================ */
function getFilteredColumns() {
  const t = tables[activeTable];
  if (!t) return [];
  return activeFilter === 'all'
    ? t.columns.map((c, i) => ({ col: c, realIdx: i }))
    : t.columns.map((c, i) => ({ col: c, realIdx: i })).filter(({ col }) => FIELD_TYPES[col.type]?.category === activeFilter);
}

function renderTable() {
  const tbody = document.getElementById('table-body');
  const filtered = getFilteredColumns();
  updateColCountLabel();

  if (filtered.length === 0) {
    tbody.innerHTML = `<tr><td colspan="6" class="table-empty">No columns in this category.</td></tr>`;
    renderAddRow();
    return;
  }

  tbody.innerHTML = filtered.map(({ col, realIdx }) => renderTableRow(col, realIdx)).join('');

  // Re-render the add row at the bottom
  renderAddRow();

  // Restore selection highlight
  if (activeColIdx !== null) {
    const row = tbody.querySelector(`tr[data-idx="${activeColIdx}"]`);
    if (row) row.classList.add('selected');
  }
}

function renderTableRow(col, idx) {
  const ft = FIELD_TYPES[col.type] || {};
  const t = tables[activeTable];
  const isFirst = idx === 0;
  const isLast  = idx === t.columns.length - 1;

  return `
    <tr data-idx="${idx}" onclick="selectRow(${idx})" class="${activeColIdx === idx ? 'selected' : ''}">
      <td class="td-num">
        <span class="row-num" style="color:var(--text-dim);font:500 11px var(--font-mono)">${idx + 1}</span>
        <span class="row-expand">⤢</span>
      </td>
      <td>
        <div class="td-name">
          <span class="col-icon">${ft.icon || ''}</span>
          <span class="col-name-text">${escHtml(col.name)}</span>
        </div>
      </td>
      <td>
        <span class="type-chip ${ft.category || ''}">${ft.title || col.type}</span>
      </td>
      <td class="td-slug">${escHtml(col.slug || '')}</td>
      <td class="td-sql">${ft.sql || ''}</td>
      <td>
        <div class="td-actions" onclick="event.stopPropagation()">
          <button class="btn ghost icon-only sm" onclick="moveColumn(${idx}, -1)" ${isFirst ? 'disabled' : ''} title="Move up" style="${isFirst ? 'opacity:0.3' : ''}">▲</button>
          <button class="btn ghost icon-only sm" onclick="moveColumn(${idx}, 1)"  ${isLast  ? 'disabled' : ''} title="Move down" style="${isLast ? 'opacity:0.3' : ''}">▼</button>
          <button class="btn ghost icon-only sm" onclick="deleteRowDirect(${idx})" title="Delete">✕</button>
        </div>
      </td>
    </tr>
  `;
}

function renderAddRow() {
  const tbody = document.getElementById('table-body');
  const types = [
    ['hex_id','🔑 Hex ID'], ['text_single','📝 Text'], ['text_multi','📋 Multi'],
    ['int_scalar','🔢 Int'], ['float_scalar','🔢 Float'], ['boolean','🔘 Bool'],
    ['enum_single','🏷️ Enum'], ['enum_multi','🏷️ Multi-Enum'],
    ['relation_single','🔗 Relation'], ['relation_multi','🔗 Rel-N'],
  ];
  const existingAddRow = tbody.querySelector('.row-add');
  if (existingAddRow) existingAddRow.remove();

  const tr = document.createElement('tr');
  tr.className = 'row-add';
  tr.innerHTML = `<td colspan="6">
    <div class="add-field-strip">
      <span style="font:600 11px var(--font-mono);color:var(--text-dim);margin-right:0.25rem;">+ ADD</span>
      ${types.map(([slug, label]) => `
        <button class="add-chip" onclick="addField('${slug}')">${label}</button>
      `).join('')}
    </div>
  </td>`;
  tbody.appendChild(tr);
}

/* ============================================================
   ROW SELECTION → SIDEBAR
   ============================================================ */
function selectRow(idx) {
  if (activeColIdx === idx) {
    // Toggle: clicking same row closes sidebar
    closeSidebar();
    return;
  }
  activeColIdx = idx;

  // Update row highlight
  document.querySelectorAll('#table-body tr').forEach(r => r.classList.remove('selected'));
  const row = document.querySelector(`#table-body tr[data-idx="${idx}"]`);
  if (row) row.classList.add('selected');

  openSidebar();
}

function openSidebar() {
  document.getElementById('field-sidebar').classList.add('open');
  populateSidebar();
}

function closeSidebar() {
  document.getElementById('field-sidebar').classList.remove('open');
  document.querySelectorAll('#table-body tr').forEach(r => r.classList.remove('selected'));
  activeColIdx = null;
}

function navigateSidebar(dir) {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  const t = tables[activeTable];
  const next = activeColIdx + dir;
  if (next < 0 || next >= t.columns.length) return;
  activeColIdx = next;

  document.querySelectorAll('#table-body tr').forEach(r => r.classList.remove('selected'));
  const row = document.querySelector(`#table-body tr[data-idx="${next}"]`);
  if (row) row.classList.add('selected');

  populateSidebar();
}

/* ============================================================
   SIDEBAR POPULATION
   ============================================================ */
function populateSidebar() {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  const t = tables[activeTable];
  const col = t.columns[activeColIdx];
  if (!col) return;
  const ft = FIELD_TYPES[col.type] || {};

  // Header labels
  document.getElementById('sb-col-num').textContent   = `#${activeColIdx + 1} of ${t.columns.length}`;
  document.getElementById('sb-col-icon').textContent  = ft.icon || '';
  document.getElementById('sb-col-title').textContent = col.name;

  // Edit fields
  document.getElementById('sb-name').value = col.name;
  document.getElementById('sb-slug').value = col.slug || '';

  // Type select
  const sel = document.getElementById('sb-type');
  sel.innerHTML = Object.entries(FIELD_TYPES).map(([slug, info]) =>
    `<option value="${slug}" ${col.type === slug ? 'selected' : ''}>${info.icon} ${info.title}</option>`
  ).join('');

  // Meta section
  renderSidebarMeta(col);

  // Code panels
  populateSidebarCode();
}

function renderSidebarMeta(col) {
  const meta = col.metadata || {};
  const container = document.getElementById('sb-meta');

  if (col.type === 'hex_id') {
    container.innerHTML = `
      <div class="field-group">
        <label class="field-label">ID Prefix <span class="field-hint">(max 4 chars)</span></label>
        <input type="text" maxlength="4" value="${escHtml(meta.prefix || '')}"
          oninput="sbUpdateMeta('prefix', this.value)">
      </div>
    `;
    return;
  }

  if (col.type.startsWith('enum_')) {
    const options = Array.isArray(meta.options) ? meta.options : [];
    container.innerHTML = `
      <div class="field-group">
        <label class="field-label">Options</label>
        <div class="options-list" id="sb-options-list">
          ${options.map((opt, i) => `
            <span class="option-pill">
              ${escHtml(opt)}
              <button onclick="sbRemoveOption(${i})" title="Remove">✕</button>
            </span>
          `).join('')}
        </div>
        <input type="text" placeholder="Type option, press Enter"
          onkeydown="if(event.key==='Enter'){sbAddOption(this.value);this.value='';}" style="margin-top:0.4rem;">
      </div>
    `;
    return;
  }

  if (col.type.startsWith('relation_')) {
    const target = meta.target || 'self';
    container.innerHTML = `
      <div class="field-group">
        <label class="field-label">Target Table</label>
        <select onchange="sbUpdateMeta('target', this.value)">
          <option value="self" ${target === 'self' ? 'selected' : ''}>Self (tree)</option>
          ${Object.keys(tables).map(tname => `
            <option value="${tname}" ${target === tname ? 'selected' : ''}>${tname}</option>
          `).join('')}
        </select>
      </div>
    `;
    return;
  }

  container.innerHTML = '';
}

function populateSidebarCode() {
  const t = tables[activeTable];
  document.getElementById('sql-title').textContent  = `${t.table_name}.sql`;
  document.getElementById('json-title').textContent = `${t.table_name}.json`;
  document.getElementById('sql-code').textContent   = generateSQL(t);
  document.getElementById('json-code').textContent  = JSON.stringify(t, null, 2);
}

/* ============================================================
   SIDEBAR TAB SWITCHING
   ============================================================ */
function switchSidebarTab(tab, btn) {
  activeSidebarTab = tab;
  document.querySelectorAll('.stab-btn').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
  btn.classList.add('active');
  document.querySelectorAll('.sidebar-panel').forEach(p => p.classList.remove('active'));
  document.getElementById(`sp-${tab}`).classList.add('active');
  if (tab === 'sql' || tab === 'json') populateSidebarCode();
}

/* ============================================================
   SIDEBAR MUTATION HANDLERS
   ============================================================ */
function sbUpdateName(val) {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].name = val;
  document.getElementById('sb-col-title').textContent = val;
  refreshTableRow(activeColIdx);
  renderTokenStrip();
}

function sbUpdateSlug(val) {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].slug = val;
  refreshTableRow(activeColIdx);
}

function sbUpdateType(val) {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  const col = tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx];
  col.type = val;
  col.metadata = {};
  if (val.startsWith('enum_'))     col.metadata.options = ['option1'];
  if (val.startsWith('relation_')) col.metadata.target  = 'self';
  if (val === 'hex_id')            col.metadata.prefix  = activeTable.substring(0, 4).toUpperCase();
  populateSidebar();
  refreshTableRow(activeColIdx);
}

function sbUpdateMeta(key, val) {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  if (!tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].metadata)
    tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].metadata = {};
  tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].metadata[key] = val;
}

function sbAddOption(val) {
  if (!val.trim() || activeColIdx === null) return;
  const meta = tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].metadata;
  if (!Array.isArray(meta.options)) meta.options = [];
  if (!meta.options.includes(val)) { meta.options.push(val); }
  renderSidebarMeta(tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx]);
}

function sbRemoveOption(i) {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].metadata.options.splice(i, 1);
  renderSidebarMeta(tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx]);
}

function sbDeleteColumn() {
  if (activeColIdx === null) return;
  const name = tables[activeTable].columns[activeColIdx].name;
  tables[activeTable].columns.splice(activeColIdx, 1);
  closeSidebar();
  renderTable();
  renderTokenStrip();
  updateColCountLabel();
  showToast(`Deleted "${name}"`);
}

/* ============================================================
   TABLE ROW ACTIONS (from action cell, not sidebar)
   ============================================================ */
function deleteRowDirect(idx) {
  const name = tables[activeTable].columns[idx].name;
  tables[activeTable].columns.splice(idx, 1);
  if (activeColIdx === idx) closeSidebar();
  else if (activeColIdx !== null && activeColIdx > idx) activeColIdx--;
  renderTable();
  renderTokenStrip();
  updateColCountLabel();
  showToast(`Deleted "${name}"`);
}

function moveColumn(idx, dir) {
  const cols = tables[activeTable].columns;
  const target = idx + dir;
  if (target < 0 || target >= cols.length) return;

  const [moved] = cols.splice(idx, 1);
  cols.splice(target, 0, moved);

  // Track sidebar selection
  if      (activeColIdx === idx)    activeColIdx = target;
  else if (activeColIdx === target) activeColIdx = idx;

  renderTable();
  renderTokenStrip();
  if (activeColIdx !== null) populateSidebar();
}

function addField(type) {
  const t = tables[activeTable];
  const newCol = { name: FIELD_TYPES[type].title, slug: 'new_field', type, metadata: {} };
  if (type.startsWith('enum_'))     newCol.metadata.options = ['option1', 'option2'];
  if (type.startsWith('relation_')) newCol.metadata.target  = 'self';
  if (type === 'hex_id')            newCol.metadata.prefix  = activeTable.substring(0, 4).toUpperCase();
  t.columns.push(newCol);
  renderTable();
  renderTokenStrip();
  updateColCountLabel();
  // Open sidebar on new column
  activeColIdx = t.columns.length - 1;
  openSidebar();
  showToast(`Added ${FIELD_TYPES[type].title}`);
}

/* Refresh a single table row in-place without full re-render */
function refreshTableRow(idx) {
  const col = tables[activeTable].columns[idx];
  const row = document.querySelector(`#table-body tr[data-idx="${idx}"]`);
  if (!row) { renderTable(); return; }
  const ft = FIELD_TYPES[col.type] || {};

  row.querySelector('.col-icon').textContent      = ft.icon || '';
  row.querySelector('.col-name-text').textContent = col.name;
  const chip = row.querySelector('.type-chip');
  chip.className = `type-chip ${ft.category || ''}`;
  chip.textContent = ft.title || col.type;
  row.querySelector('.td-slug').textContent = col.slug || '';
  row.querySelector('.td-sql').textContent  = ft.sql || '';
}

/* ============================================================
   TOKEN STRIP (drag-to-reorder column chips above table)
   ============================================================ */
function renderTokenStrip() {
  if (!tables[activeTable]) return;
  const strip = document.getElementById('token-strip');

  const CAT_COLORS = {
    pk: 'var(--c-pk)', text: 'var(--c-text)', scalar: 'var(--c-scalar)',
    boolean: 'var(--c-boolean)', enum: 'var(--c-enum)', rel: 'var(--c-rel)',
  };

  strip.innerHTML = tables[activeTable].columns.map((col, idx) => {
    const ft   = FIELD_TYPES[col.type] || {};
    const color = CAT_COLORS[ft.category] || 'var(--accent)';
    return `
      <div class="col-chip" data-index="${idx}">
        <span class="chip-handle">⋮⋮</span>
        <span class="chip-dot" style="background:${color};"></span>
        <span>${escHtml(col.name)}</span>
      </div>
    `;
  }).join('');

  strip.querySelectorAll('.col-chip').forEach(chip => {
    chip.addEventListener('pointerdown', handleChipPointerDown);
  });
}

/* ---- Pointer drag engine (FLIP) ---- */
let activeDrag = null;

function handleChipPointerDown(e) {
  if (e.button !== 0) return;
  const chip    = e.currentTarget;
  const strip   = document.getElementById('token-strip');
  const fromIdx = Number(chip.dataset.index);
  const rect    = chip.getBoundingClientRect();

  chip.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);

  const placeholder  = document.createElement('div');
  placeholder.className = 'chip-placeholder';
  placeholder.style.width  = `${rect.width}px`;
  placeholder.style.height = `${rect.height}px`;

  const offsetX = e.clientX - rect.left;
  const offsetY = e.clientY - rect.top;

  activeDrag = { chip, strip, fromIdx, placeholder, offsetX, offsetY,
                 rect, isDragging: false, startX: e.clientX, startY: e.clientY };

  const onMove = (me) => {
    if (!activeDrag) return;
    const dist = Math.hypot(me.clientX - activeDrag.startX, me.clientY - activeDrag.startY);

    if (!activeDrag.isDragging && dist > 3) {
      activeDrag.isDragging = true;
      chip.parentNode.insertBefore(placeholder, chip);
      chip.classList.add('is-dragging');
      chip.style.width  = `${rect.width}px`;
      chip.style.height = `${rect.height}px`;
    }

    if (activeDrag.isDragging) {
      chip.style.left = `${me.clientX - offsetX}px`;
      chip.style.top  = `${me.clientY - offsetY}px`;
      updateChipPlacementFLIP(me.clientX, me.clientY);
    }
  };

  const onUp = () => {
    window.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
    window.removeEventListener('pointerup', onUp);
    try { chip.releasePointerCapture(e.pointerId); } catch (_) {}

    if (!activeDrag.isDragging) { activeDrag = null; return; }

    const targetRect  = placeholder.getBoundingClientRect();
    const currentLeft = parseFloat(chip.style.left);
    const currentTop  = parseFloat(chip.style.top);
    const dx = targetRect.left - currentLeft;
    const dy = targetRect.top  - currentTop;

    chip.style.transition = 'transform 0.22s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)';
    chip.style.transform  = `translate(${dx}px,${dy}px)`;

    setTimeout(() => {
      const children = [...strip.children].filter(c => c !== chip);
      const toIdx    = children.indexOf(placeholder);

      chip.classList.remove('is-dragging');
      ['position','left','top','width','height','transform','transition','boxShadow']
        .forEach(p => chip.style[p] = '');

      if (placeholder.parentNode) placeholder.parentNode.removeChild(placeholder);

      if (toIdx !== -1 && toIdx !== activeDrag.fromIdx) {
        const cols = tables[activeTable].columns;
        const [movedCol] = cols.splice(activeDrag.fromIdx, 1);
        cols.splice(toIdx, 0, movedCol);

        // Remap sidebar selection
        if (activeColIdx !== null) {
          if      (activeColIdx === activeDrag.fromIdx) activeColIdx = toIdx;
          else if (activeDrag.fromIdx < toIdx && activeColIdx > activeDrag.fromIdx && activeColIdx <= toIdx) activeColIdx--;
          else if (activeDrag.fromIdx > toIdx && activeColIdx >= toIdx && activeColIdx < activeDrag.fromIdx) activeColIdx++;
        }

        renderTable();
        renderTokenStrip();
        if (activeColIdx !== null) { openSidebar(); populateSidebar(); }
      }
      activeDrag = null;
    }, 220);
  };

  window.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
  window.addEventListener('pointerup', onUp);
}

function updateChipPlacementFLIP(pX, pY) {
  const { strip, chip, placeholder } = activeDrag;
  const elements = [...strip.querySelectorAll('.col-chip:not(.is-dragging)')];
  let target = null;

  for (const el of elements) {
    const box = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (pY < box.top - 4)                                    { target = el; break; }
    if (pY <= box.bottom + 4 && pX < box.left + box.width/2) { target = el; break; }
  }

  const curr = placeholder.nextElementSibling === chip ? chip.nextElementSibling : placeholder.nextElementSibling;
  if (curr === target) return;

  const firstPos = new Map();
  elements.forEach(el => firstPos.set(el, el.getBoundingClientRect()));

  if (target) strip.insertBefore(placeholder, target);
  else        strip.appendChild(placeholder);

  elements.forEach(el => {
    const first = firstPos.get(el);
    const last  = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    const dx = first.left - last.left;
    const dy = first.top  - last.top;
    if (dx !== 0 || dy !== 0) {
      el.style.transition = 'none';
      el.style.transform  = `translate(${dx}px,${dy}px)`;
      el.offsetHeight; // force reflow
      el.style.transition = 'transform 0.22s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1)';
      el.style.transform  = '';
    }
  });
}

/* ============================================================
   CODE GENERATION
   ============================================================ */
function generateSQL(table) {
  if (!table) return '-- No table';
  const lines = [`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ${table.table_name} (`];
  const cols = table.columns.map(col => {
    const ft = FIELD_TYPES[col.type];
    return `    ${(col.slug || col.name).padEnd(22)} ${ft.sql}`;
  });
  lines.push(cols.join(',\n'));
  lines.push(');');
  return lines.join('\n');
}

/* ============================================================
   MISC
   ============================================================ */
function copyCode(elId) {
  const text = document.getElementById(elId).textContent;
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(() => showToast('Copied!'));
}

function saveTable() {
  localStorage.setItem('project_entry_schemas', JSON.stringify(tables));
  showToast('Saved to local storage');
}

function syncSqlite() {
  showToast('SQLite sync (standalone mode)');
}

function toggleTheme() {
  const cur = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme') || 'system';
  const next = cur === 'dark' ? 'light' : cur === 'light' ? 'system' : 'dark';
  if (next === 'system') document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');
  else document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', next);
}

function showToast(msg) {
  const toast = document.getElementById('toast');
  toast.textContent = msg;
  toast.classList.add('show');
  setTimeout(() => toast.classList.remove('show'), 2400);
}

function escHtml(str) {
  return String(str)
    .replace(/&/g, '&')
    .replace(/</g, '<')
    .replace(/>/g, '>')
    .replace(/"/g, '"');
}

/* ============================================================
   BOOT
   ============================================================ */
init();
</script>
</body>
</html>

      --radius-md: 8px;

      --bg-canvas:      #faf8f5;
      --bg-card:        #fff8f3;
      --bg-card-hover:  #fff0e8;

        --border-light:   #e8dccf;
        --border-mid:     #d9cabc;

        --accent:         #d97706;
        --accent-hover:   #b45309;
        --accent-bg:      rgba(217, 119, 6, 0.10);
        color-scheme: light;
      }
    }

       RESET
       ======================================================================== */

      width: 1px;

    /* Table tabs */
    .table-tabs {

    .tab-btn {
      padding: 0.4rem 0.9rem;

      background: transparent;
      border: 1px solid transparent;

      color: var(--text-tertiary);
      cursor: pointer;
      transition: all 0.12s ease;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 0.4rem;
      outline: none;

      background: var(--bg-input);
      color: var(--text-secondary);
      border-color: var(--border-light);

      background: var(--accent-bg);
      border-color: var(--accent);
      color: var(--accent);
      font-weight: 600;
    }

    .tab-btn.new-table {
      border-style: dashed;
      border-color: var(--border-mid);
      color: var(--text-dim);
    }

    .tab-btn.new-table:hover {
      border-color: var(--accent);
      color: var(--accent);
      background: var(--accent-bg);

    /* Header actions */
    .header-actions {
      display: flex;
      gap: 0.5rem;
      flex-shrink: 0;
    }

    /* ========================================================================
       BUTTONS
